verdict.rationale: Fellow's ReadMe-hosted API reference has a live "Try It!" request panel on every endpoint page and is backed by an OpenAPI 3.1 document, so the core of an interactive, runnable reference exists. The documented limitations are real: requests run only against the live workspace, require a paid plan and admin enablement of the API, and no sandbox or test workspace is offered. Missing for 10: a sandbox or test workspace for safe runnable examples, ungated access to try requests, a Fellow-branded downloadable spec, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the Try It experience.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: Fellow's ReadMe-hosted API reference runs a live "Try It!" request panel on every endpoint page, with llms.txt and per-page .md mirrors.
Requests run against the live workspace (https://{subdomain}.fellow.app/api/v1/...) behind the paid-plan and workspace-admin enablement gates recorded in the help-article row.
Fellow's Developer API is described by an OpenAPI 3.1 document
The API Reference and Developer Guide is available at: https://developers.fellow.ai/
